newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end sharply up as heavyweights gain.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end sharply up as heavyweights gain.

text.p: Dutch shares ended with strong gains on Wednesday, helped by advances at heavyweights ABN AMRO, ING, Royal Dutch and KLM, outweighing a fall at Hoogovens.

The AEX index of leading shares closed 13.30 points higher at 992.89, off an intra-day peak of 995.42. The move upward, a reversal after a period of sideways trade take the market closer to its all-time record of 1006.26, scored on July 23.

Early buying was noted in flag carrier KLM, which surprised the market with Q1 profits on Tuesday of 244 million guilders. Some analysts raised their estimates on Wednesday and the shares ended 3.90 guilders up at 79.90 as a result.
Oil giant Royal Dutch put on 1.30 guilders to close at 120.20, helped by the strong dollar ahead of its results due tomorrow. Shell in London ended with similar-sized gains.

Stocks were helped by a bond market, which improved steadily through the day, and in turn lifted financials in particular. Banking groups ABN AMRO and ING were among the most heavily-traded stocks, finishing 1.70 and 2.30 guilders firmer at 48.90 and 99.80 respectively.
The results spotlight turned to Hoogovens in the afternoon, which announced a 40 percent leap in first half net profits to 194 million guilders, pushing the shares initially higher.
But Hoogovens, which had attracted heavy buying ahead of the results, fell back as analysts digested an extraordinary gain of 13 million guilders in the figures.
"They looked good at the start but it's the extraordinary gain -- if you strip the 13 million guilders out then they lose their shine," one dealer said.
The shares hit a high at 142.30 guilders before reversing and ending at 132.80, a drop of 3.20 guilders on the day.
Food and bio-tech group Gist-Brocades lost more ground after a dramatic 14-guilder slide on Tuesday linked to a profit warning. It ended another 1.10 guilders off at 63.80.
